metadata.title: A strong convergence result involving an inertial forward-backward algorithm for monotone inclusions

items.name: Definition 2.1
items.statement:
Definition 2.1. A mapping $T: C \to C$ is said to be nonexpansive if

$$
\| T x - T y \| \leq \| x - y \|, \forall x, y \in C.
$$

items.name: Metric projection
items.statement:
For any point $u \in H$ , there exists a unique point $P_C u \in C$ such that

$$
| | u - P _ {C} u | | \leq | | u - y | |, \forall y \in C.
$$

$P_{C}$ is called the metric projection of $H$ onto $C$ . We know that $P_{C}$ is a nonexpansive mapping of $H$ onto $C$ . It is also known that $P_{C}$ satisfies

$$
\langle x - y, P _ {C} x - P _ {C} y \rangle \geq | | P _ {C} x - P _ {C} y | | ^ {2}, \tag {2.1}
$$

for all $x, y \in H$ . Furthermore, $P_{C}x$ is characterized by the properties $P_{C}x \in C$ and

$$
\langle x - P _ {C} x, P _ {C} x - y \rangle \geq 0, \tag {2.2}
$$

for all $y \in C$ . We also know that all Hilbert space has the Kadec-Klee property, that is, $\{x_n\}$ converges weakly to $x$ and $\| x_n \| \to \| x \|$ imply $\{x_n\}$ converges strongly to $x$ .

items.name: Definition 2.3(b): strongly monotone operator
items.statement:
A nonlinear operator $A$ is $\beta$-strongly monotone on its domain $D(A)$ if there exists $\beta>0$ such that

$$
\langle x-y,Ax-Ay\rangle \geq \beta\|x-y\|^2,\qquad \forall x,y\in D(A).
$$

items.name: Pointwise operator sum and its zero set
items.statement:
For a single-valued operator $A:H\to H$ and a set-valued operator $B:H\rightrightarrows H$, define

$$
(A+B)(x)=\{Ax+b:b\in Bx\},
$$

and

$$
(A+B)^{-1}(0)=\{x\in H:0\in Ax+Bx\}.
$$

This is the solution set of the monotone inclusion (1.1).

items.name: Lemma 2.5 (Sahu et al. [55])
items.statement:
Lemma 2.5. (Sahu et al. [55]) Let $C$ be a closed and convex subset of a real Hilbert space $H$ . For any $x, y, z \in H$ , and a real number $a \in \mathbb{R}$ , the set

$$
\{v \in C: | | y - v | | ^ {2} \leq | | x - v | | ^ {2} + \langle z, v \rangle + a \}
$$

is closed and convex.
items.proof: Cited from: Sahu, D.R., Xu, H.-K., Yao, J.C.: Asymptotically strictly pseudocontractive mappings in the intermediate sense. Nonlinear Anal. 70, 3502-3511 (2009).

items.name: Iterative method (3.1)
items.statement:
Let $H$ be a real Hilbert space. Let $A:H\to H$ be an $\alpha$ -ism and $B:H\to 2^{H}$ a maximal monotone operator such that $\Omega := (A + B)^{-1}(0)\neq \emptyset$ . Let $\{\alpha_n\} \subset \mathbb{R}$ and let a sequence $\{x_{n}\}_{n = 0}^{\infty}$ in $H$ be generated by $x_0,x_1\in H$ and for all $n\geq 1$ ,

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} y _ {n} = x _ {n} + \alpha_ {n} (x _ {n} - x _ {n - 1}), \\ z _ {n} = (I + r _ {n} B) ^ {- 1} (y _ {n} - r _ {n} A y _ {n}), \\ C _ {n} = \{u \in H: | | z _ {n} - u | | ^ {2} \leq | | x _ {n} - u | | ^ {2} - 2 \alpha_ {n} \langle x _ {n} - u, x _ {n - 1} - x _ {n} \rangle \\ \quad + \alpha_ {n} ^ {2} | | x _ {n - 1} - x _ {n} | | ^ {2} \}, \\ Q _ {n} = \{u \in H: \langle u - x _ {n}, x _ {0} - x _ {n} \rangle \leq 0 \}, \\ x _ {n + 1} = P _ {C _ {n} \cap Q _ {n}} (x _ {0}). \end{array} \right. \tag {3.1}
$$

items.name: Definition 2.2
items.statement:
Definition 2.2. A mapping $T: H \to H$ is said to be firmly nonexpansive if and only if $2T - I$ is nonexpansive, or equivalently

$$
\langle x - y, T x - T y \rangle \geq | | T x - T y | | ^ {2}, \forall x, y \in H.
$$

Alternatively, $T$ is firmly nonexpansive if and only if $T$ can be expressed as

$$
T = \frac {1}{2} (I + S),
$$

where $S:H\to H$ is nonexpansive. Projections are firmly nonexpansive.

items.name: Lemma 2.6 (Lopez et al. [34])
items.statement:
Lemma 2.6. (Lopez et al. [34]) Let E be a real Banach space. Let $A: H \to 2^{H}$ be a maximal monotone operator and $B: H \to H$ be an $\alpha$ -inverse strongly monotone mapping on H. Define $T_{r} := (I + rB)^{-1}(x - rAx)$ , r > 0. Then we have,

(i) for $r > 0$ , $F(T_r) = (A + B)^{-1}(0)$ .  
(ii) for $0 < s \leq r$ and $x \in E$ , $||x - T_s x|| \leq 2 ||x - T_r x||$ .
items.proof: Cited from: Lopez, G., Martin-Marquez, V., Wang, F., Xu, H.-K.: Forward-Backward splitting methods for accretive operators in Banach spaces. Abstr. Appl. Anal. 2012 (2010). Article ID 109236.

items.name: Lemma 2.7 (Browder [16])
items.statement: Lemma 2.7. (Browder [16]) Let C be a nonempty closed convex subset of a Hilbert space H and T a nonexpansive mapping with $F(T) \neq \emptyset$ . If $\{x_{n}\}$ is a sequence in C such that $x_{n} \rightharpoonup x$ and $(I - T)x_{n} \to y$ , then $(I - T)x = y$ . In particular, if y = 0, then $x \in F(T)$ .
items.proof: Cited from: Browder, F.E.: Nonexpansive nonlinear operators in a Banach space. Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 54, 1041-1044 (1965).

items.name: Forward-backward nonexpansiveness and fixed points
items.statement:
Let $A:H\to H$ be $\alpha$-inverse strongly monotone and let $B:H\rightrightarrows H$ be maximal monotone. For $0<\varepsilon\leq 2\alpha$, any single-valued realization

$$
T_\varepsilon x\in (I+\varepsilon B)^{-1}(x-\varepsilon Ax)
$$

is nonexpansive and its fixed-point set is exactly $(A+B)^{-1}(0)$. This is the forward-backward fact invoked in the proof of Theorem 3.2.

items.name: Lemma 2.4
items.statement:
Lemma 2.4. Let $C$ be a nonempty closed convex subset of a real Hilbert space $H$ and $P_C: H \to C$ be the metric projection from $H$ onto $C$ . Then the following inequality holds:

$$
| | y - P _ {C} x | | ^ {2} + | | x - P _ {C} x | | ^ {2} \leq | | x - y | | ^ {2}, \quad \forall x \in H, \forall y \in C.
$$

items.name: Remark 3.1
items.statement:
Remark 3.1. We make the following remarks about our iterative method (3.1).

(1) We observe that for any $u \in H$ ,

$$
\begin{array}{l} | | z _ {n} - u | | ^ {2} \leq | | x _ {n} - u | | ^ {2} - 2 \alpha_ {n} \langle x _ {n} - u, x _ {n - 1} - x _ {n} \rangle + \alpha_ {n} ^ {2} | | x _ {n - 1} - x _ {n} | | ^ {2} \\ \Leftrightarrow \\ \| z _ {n} \| ^ {2} - 2 \langle u, z _ {n} \rangle \leq \| x _ {n} \| ^ {2} - 2 \langle u, x _ {n} \rangle + 2 \alpha_ {n} \langle u, x _ {n - 1} - x _ {n} \rangle \\ - 2 \alpha_ {n} \langle x _ {n}, x _ {n - 1} - x _ {n} \rangle + \alpha_ {n} ^ {2} | | x _ {n - 1} - x _ {n} | | ^ {2} \\ \Leftrightarrow \\ 2 \langle u, x _ {n} - z _ {n} - \alpha_ {n} (x _ {n - 1} - x _ {n}) \rangle \leq \| x _ {n} \| ^ {2} - \| z _ {n} \| ^ {2} \\ - 2 \alpha_ {n} \langle x _ {n}, x _ {n - 1} - x _ {n} \rangle + \alpha_ {n} ^ {2} | | x _ {n - 1} - x _ {n} | | ^ {2} \\ \Leftrightarrow \\ 2 \langle u, y _ {n} - z _ {n} \rangle \leq \| x _ {n} \| ^ {2} - \| z _ {n} \| ^ {2} - 2 \alpha_ {n} \langle x _ {n}, x _ {n - 1} - x _ {n} \rangle + \alpha_ {n} ^ {2} \| x _ {n - 1} - x _ {n} \| ^ {2} \\ \Leftrightarrow \\ \langle u, x _ {n} - z _ {n} \rangle \leq \frac {1}{2} \Big [ \| x _ {n} \| ^ {2} - \| z _ {n} \| ^ {2} - 2 \alpha_ {n} \langle x _ {n}, x _ {n - 1} - x _ {n} \rangle + \alpha_ {n} ^ {2} \| x _ {n - 1} - x _ {n} \| ^ {2} \Big ]. \end{array}
$$

Therefore, the set $C_{n}$ defined in our iterative method (3.1) is a half space. Hence, the metric projection $P_{C_{n}}$ has a closed-form expression and can be easily computed (see [19]).

(2) For any $u \in H$ ,

$$
\begin{array}{l} \langle u - x _ {n}, x _ {0} - x _ {n} \rangle \leq 0 \\ \Leftrightarrow \langle u, x _ {0} - x _ {n} \rangle \leq \langle x _ {n}, x _ {0} - x _ {n} \rangle . \end{array}
$$

Therefore, the set $Q_{n}$ defined in iterative method (3.1) is a half space and the metric projection $P_{Q_{n}}$ has a closed-form expression and can also be easily computed.

(3) Since both $C_n$ and $Q_n$ are half-spaces, then the closed-form expressions for the projections onto the intersection of two half-spaces $C_n$ and $Q_n$ are given in Propositions 28.18 and 28.19 of [6]. Therefore, the iterate $x_{n+1}$ in our iterative method (3.1) can be easily computed.

items.name: Theorem 3.2
items.statement: Theorem 3.2. Let $H$ be a real Hilbert space. Let $A: H \to H$ be an $\alpha$ -ism and $B: H \to 2^H$ a maximal monotone operator such that $\Omega := (A + B)^{-1}(0) \neq \emptyset$ . Let $\{\alpha_n\}$ be a bounded real sequence. Let a sequence $\{x_n\}_{n=0}^{\infty}$ in $H$ be generated by (3.1). If $0 < \liminf_{n \to \infty} r_n \leq \limsup_{n \to \infty} r_n < 2\alpha$ , then $\{x_n\}_{n=0}^{\infty}$ converges strongly to $\overline{x} = P_{\Omega}x_0$ .
items.proof:
Proof. We divide our proof into these steps.

Step 1 Show that $\{x_{n}\}_{n = 0}^{\infty}$ is well defined and $\Omega \subset C_n\cap Q_n,\forall n\geq 0$

By Lemma 2.5, it is obvious that $C_n$ is closed and convex for all $n \geq 0$ . Furthermore, $Q_n$ is closed and convex for all $n \geq 0$ . So, $C_n \cap Q_n$ is closed and convex for all $n \geq 0$ .

Let $u \in \Omega$ . Then by a direct computation, we obtain,

$$
\begin{array}{l} | | y _ {n} - u | | ^ {2} = | | (x _ {n} - u) - \alpha_ {n} (x _ {n - 1} - x _ {n}) | | ^ {2} \\ = | | x _ {n} - u | | ^ {2} - 2 \alpha_ {n} \langle x _ {n} - u, x _ {n - 1} - x _ {n} \rangle + \alpha_ {n} ^ {2} | | x _ {n - 1} - x _ {n} | | ^ {2}. \end{array}
$$

Furthermore, we have,

$$
\begin{array}{l} | | z _ {n} - u | | ^ {2} = | | (I + r _ {n} B) ^ {- 1} (y _ {n} - r _ {n} A y _ {n}) - (I + r _ {n} B) ^ {- 1} (u - r _ {n} A u) | | ^ {2} \\ \leq | | y _ {n} - u - r _ {n} (A y _ {n} - A u) | | ^ {2} \\ = | | y _ {n} - u | | ^ {2} - 2 r _ {n} \langle A y _ {n} - A u, y _ {n} - u \rangle + r _{n} ^ {2} | | A y _ {n} - A u | | ^ {2} \\ \leq | | y _ {n} - u | | ^ {2} - 2 r _ {n} \alpha | | A y _ {n} - A u | | ^ {2} + r _ {n} ^ {2} | | A y _ {n} - A u | | ^ {2} \\ = | | y _ {n} - u | | ^ {2} - (2 \alpha - r _ {n}) r _ {n} | | A y _ {n} - A u | | ^ {2} \leq | | y _ {n} - u | | ^ {2} \\ = | | x _ {n} - u | | ^ {2} - 2 \alpha_ {n} \langle x _ {n} - u, x _ {n -1} - x _ {n} \rangle + \alpha_ {n} ^ {2} | | x _ {n - 1} - x _ {n} | | ^ {2}. \end{array}
$$

Therefore, $u \in C_n$ , $\forall n \geq 1$ . Clearly, $u \in C_0$ . So, $u \in C_n$ , $\forall n \geq 0$ . Thus, $\Omega \subset C_n$ , $\forall n \geq 0$ . For $n = 0$ , we have that $x_0 \in H$ and $Q_0 = H$ and hence $\Omega \subset H = C_0 \cap Q_0$ . Suppose that $x_k$ is given and $\Omega \subset C_k \cap Q_k$ for some $k \in \{0, 1, 2, \ldots\}$ . Since $C_k \cap Q_k$ is nonempty, closed and convex, there exists a unique element $x_{k+1} \in C_k \cap Q_k$ such that $x_{k+1} = P_{C_k \cap Q_k}(x_0)$ . It follows that,

$$
\langle z - x _ {k + 1}, x _ {0} - x _ {k + 1} \rangle \leq 0, \forall z \in C _ {k} \cap Q _ {k}.
$$

Since $\Omega \subset C_k \cap Q_k$ , we have in particular that,

$$
\langle z - x _ {k + 1}, x _ {0} - x _ {k + 1} \rangle \leq 0, \forall z \in \Omega .
$$

This implies that $\Omega \subset C_{k + 1}$ . Hence $\Omega \subset C_{k + 1} \cap Q_{k + 1}$ . By induction, $\Omega \subset C_n \cap Q_n$ , $\forall n \geq 0$ and $\{x_n\}_{n=0}^{\infty}$ is well defined.

Step 2 Show that $\{x_{n}\}_{n = 0}^{\infty}$ is bounded.

From our iterative scheme (3.1), we observe that,

$$
\langle y - x _ {n}, x _ {0} - x _ {n} \rangle \leq 0, \forall y \in Q _ {n} (n \geq 1).
$$

This implies that $x_{n} = P_{Q_{n}}(x_{0})$ and hence,

$$
| | x _ {n} - x _ {0} | | \leq | | x _ {0} - y | |, \forall y \in Q _ {n}.
$$

Since $\Omega \subset Q_n$ , we have

$$
\| x _ {n} - x _ {0} \| \leq \| x _ {0} - y \|, \forall y \in \Omega . \tag {3.2}
$$

In particular, we have (since $x_{n + 1}\in Q_n$ )

$$
\| x _ {n} - x _ {0} \| \leq \| x _ {n + 1} - x _ {0} \|. \tag {3.3}
$$

By (3.2) and (3.3), we obtain $\lim_{n\to \infty}||x_n - x_0||$ exists. This implies that $\{x_{n}\}$ is bounded.

Step 3 Show that $\lim_{n\to \infty}||x_{n + 1} - x_n|| = 0.$

By Lemma 2.4 and the fact that $x_{n} = P_{Q_{n}}(x_{0})$ , we see that,

$$
| | x _ {n + 1} - x _ {n} | | ^ {2} \leq | | x _ {n + 1} - x _ {0} | | ^ {2} - | | x _ {n} - x _ {0} | | ^ {2}.
$$

Since $\lim_{n\to \infty}||x_n - x_0||$ exists, it follows that $\lim_{n\to \infty}||x_{n + 1} - x_n|| = 0$ .

Step 4 Show that $\lim_{n\to \infty}x_n = \overline{x}$ , where $\overline{x} = P_{\Omega}(x_0)$ .

We obtain from (3.1) and Step 3 that,

$$
\| y _ {n} - x _ {n} \| = | \alpha_ {n} | \| x _ {n} - x _ {n - 1} \| \to 0, n \to \infty .
$$

Hence,

$$
\| x _ {n + 1} - y _ {n} \| \leq | | x _ {n + 1} - x _ {n} | | + \| y _ {n} - x _ {n} \| \to 0, n \to \infty .
$$

Since $x_{n + 1}\in C_n$ , we have that,

$$
\begin{array}{l} \left| \left| z _ {n} - x _ {n + 1} \right| \right| ^ {2} \leq \left| \left| x _ {n} - x _ {n + 1} \right| \right| ^ {2} - 2 \alpha_ {n} \langle x _ {n} - x _ {n + 1}, x _ {n - 1} - x _ {n} \rangle \\ + \alpha_ {n} ^ {2} | | x _ {n - 1} - x _ {n} | | ^ {2} \\ \leq \left| \left| x _ {n} - x _ {n + 1} \right| \right| ^ {2} + 2 \left| \alpha_ {n} \right| \| x _ {n} - x _ {n + 1} \| x _ {n - 1} - x _ {n} \| \\ + \alpha_ {n} ^ {2} | | x _ {n - 1} - x _ {n} | | ^ {2} \to 0, n \to \infty . \end{array}
$$

Furthermore, we have,

$$
\| z _ {n} - x _ {n} \| \leq \| z _ {n} - x _ {n + 1} \| + \| x _ {n} - x _ {n + 1} \| \to 0, n \to \infty ,
$$

and

$$
\| z _ {n} - y _ {n} \| \leq \| z _ {n} - x _ {n} \| + \| x _ {n} - y _ {n} \| \to 0, n \to \infty .
$$

Take $z_{n} := T_{n}y_{n}$ , where $T_{n} := (I + r_{n}B)^{-1}(I - r_{n}A)$ . Therefore,

$$
\| T _ {n} y _ {n} - y _ {n} \| = \| z _ {n} - y _ {n} \| \to 0, n \to \infty .
$$

Since $\liminf_{n\to \infty}r_n > 0$ , there exists $\epsilon > 0$ such that $r_n \geq \epsilon$ , $\forall n \geq 1$ . Then, by Lemma 2.6, we have,

$$
\lim _ {n \to \infty} | | T _ {\epsilon} y _ {n} - y _ {n} | | \leq 2 \lim _ {n \to \infty} | | T _ {n} y _ {n} - y _ {n} | | = 0.
$$

By Lemmas 3.3 and 3.1 of [34], $T_{\epsilon}$ is nonexpansive and $F(T_{\epsilon}) = (A + B)^{-1}(0)$ . Since $\{x_{n}\}$ is bounded, there exists a subsequence $\{x_{n_i}\}$ of $\{x_{n}\}$ such that $x_{n_i} \rightharpoonup w \in H$ . Using the fact that $\|y_n - x_n\| \to 0, n \to \infty$ and $x_{n_i} \rightharpoonup w \in H$ , we have $y_{n_i} \rightharpoonup w \in H$ . We can therefore make use of Lemma 2.7 to assure that $w \in \Omega$ .

If $\overline{x} = P_{\Omega}(x_0)$ , it follows from (3.2), the fact that $w \in \Omega$ and the lower semicontinuity of the norm that,

$$
\begin{array}{l} | | x _ {0} - \overline {{x}} | | \leq | | x _ {0} - w | | \leq \operatorname * {l i m i n f} _ {i \to \infty} | | x _ {0} - x _ {n _ {i}} | | \\ \leq \operatorname * {l i m s u p} _ {i \to \infty} | | x _ {0} - x _ {n _ {i}} | | \leq | | x _ {0} - \overline {{x}} | |. \end{array}
$$

Thus, we have that $\lim_{i\to \infty}||x_{n_i} - x_0|| = ||x_0 - w|| = ||x_0 - \overline{x}||$ . This implies that $x_{n_i}\to w = \overline{x}$ , $i\to \infty$ . It follows that $\{x_n\}$ converges weakly to $\overline{x}$ . So we have,

$$
\begin{array}{l} | | x _ {0} - \overline {{x}} | | \leq \operatorname * {l i m i n f} _ {n \to \infty} | | x _ {0} - x _ {n} | | \\ \leq \operatorname * {l i m s u p} _ {n \to \infty} | | x _ {0} - x _ {n} | | \leq | | x _ {0} - \overline {{x}} | |. \end{array}
$$

This shows that $\lim_{n\to \infty}||x_n - x_0|| = ||x_0 - \overline{x}||$ . From $x_{n}\rightharpoonup \overline{x}$ , we also have $x_{n} - x_{0}\rightharpoonup \overline{x} -x_{0}$ . Since $H$ satisfies the Kadec-Klee property, it follows that $x_{n} - x_{0}\rightarrow \overline{x} -x_{0}$ . Therefore $x_{n}\rightarrow \overline{x}$ as $n\to \infty$ . We thus complete the proof.

items.name: Corollary 3.3
items.statement:
If we take A := 0 in Theorem 3.2, then we obtain the following corollary which is new in its own right.

Corollary 3.3. Let $H$ be a real Hilbert space. Let $B: H \to 2^H$ be a maximal monotone operator such that $B^{-1}(0) \neq \emptyset$ . Let $\{\alpha_n\}$ be a bounded real sequence. Let a sequence $\{x_n\}_{n=0}^{\infty}$ in $H$ be generated by $x_0, x_1 \in H$ and for all $n \geq 1$ ,

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} y _ {n} = x _ {n} + \alpha_ {n} (x _ {n} - x _ {n - 1}), \\ z _ {n} = (I + r _ {n} B) ^ {- 1} y _ {n}, \\ C _ {n} = \{u \in H: | | z _ {n} - u | | ^ {2} \leq | | x _ {n} - u | | ^ {2} - 2 \alpha_ {n} \langle x _ {n} - u, x _ {n - 1} - x _ {n} \rangle \\ \qquad + \alpha_ {n} ^ {2} | | x _ {n - 1} - x _ {n} | | ^ {2} \}, \\ Q _ {n} = \{u \in H: \langle u - x _ {n}, x _ {0} - x _ {n} \rangle \leq 0 \}, \\ x _ {n + 1} = P _ {C _ {n} \cap Q _ {n}} (x _ {0}). \end{array} \right.
$$

If $\liminf_{n\to\infty}r_n > 0$ , then $\{x_n\}_{n=0}^{\infty}$ converges strongly to $\overline{x} = P_{\Omega}x_0$ .
